asylum

/uh-SY-lum/ — rhymes with 'why'-lum · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Asylum is official protection or safe shelter given to someone fleeing harm.

After receiving death threats for her reporting, the journalist was granted asylum in Canada.

Worked Example

When soldiers began arresting journalists in her country, Nadia fled across the border with only a backpack. Officials interviewed her, reviewed the danger she faced back home, and granted her permission to stay under the host country's protection.

Nadia received asylum — official protection from harm for someone fleeing danger. Unlike a simple 'shelter,' which is any place that keeps out weather or trouble, asylum is formal protection, often granted by a government to people escaping persecution.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

refuge: A refuge is a safe place away from danger — a cave in a storm, a quiet room in a loud house. Asylum is not a place at all but a legal grant: official protection a government gives to someone fleeing harm. You can run to a refuge; asylum must be granted.

sanctuary: A sanctuary is a protected place where no one can harm you — a wildlife sanctuary, the hushed interior of a church. Asylum is the protection itself, granted on paper by a government to a person fleeing persecution — a legal status rather than a spot on a map.

haven: A haven is a place of safety and rest — originally a harbor where ships rode out rough seas. Asylum is more formal and far more powerful: protection granted by a government to someone escaping harm. A library can be a haven from noise; only a state can grant asylum.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

danger: the possibility of being harmed

exposure: the state of being left unprotected

Where it sits · how complete the protection is — shelter → asylum → immunity

shelter vs. asylum: Shelter is weaker than asylum — any roof or cover can be a shelter, but asylum is formal protection from persecution, often granted by a government.

immunity vs. asylum: Immunity is stronger than asylum — it removes a threat entirely and permanently, while asylum protects you only within your place of safety.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — a-

prefix — a-: without, not (Greek)

root — sylum

root — sylum: right of seizure (from Greek sylon; an asylon was 'a place safe from seizure')

Put it together

Put it together: Greek asylon meant 'a place without seizure' — a- (without) + sylon (the right to seize someone), spelled -sylum in English. A place where no one could be captured naturally became a place of protection.

Where This Word Comes From

Where This Word Comes From: The Greek root syle ('the right of seizure') built no other English word; asylum is its lone survivor. In ancient Greece an asylon was a temple where that right was switched off: not even a runaway slave or a defeated soldier could be dragged out of one. A place no one can seize you from is still exactly what asylum means.
